item.title: Vrbo Guests Can Pay Fees to Get Refunds When Rain Ruins a Stay
item.description: Vrbo is testing a new way to give travelers peace of mind with a weather-guarantee option powered by WeatherPromise.

item.title: India’s Next Aviation Boom Will Be Handled by New Airports, Not Bigger Ones
item.description: India is getting multiple airports in key hubs in response to traffic growth, but any major demand disruption in a newly growing India market could lead to this model falling apart.

item.title: Prism Acquires 10 Sonder Properties to Bring Belvilla Brand to U.S.: Exclusive
item.description: Prism may list in India, but it is evolving into an India-U.S. hospitality platform, using the extended-stay demand to support its next phase of international expansion.

item.title: Loyalty, Latin America, and Premium Leisure: What to Watch in IAG’s Annual Results
item.description: Airline earnings season often reveals more through comparison than individual results. On Friday, IAG will be the second of Europe’s big three to report, offering valuable insight into the health of the industry.

item.title: Trip.com Group Points to Massive Inbound Tourism Opportunity in China
item.description: Trip.com Group's earnings revealed a major opportunity in China’s underdeveloped inbound tourism market, but the company now faces a familiar risk: an antitrust investigation that could reshape platform economics and growth expectations.

item.title: How to Read Travel Subscription Earnings: The eDreams Q3 Case Study
item.description: eDreams's Q3 results require reading between the lines: what it emphasizes matters less than what it doesn’t.

item.title: The Travel Industry Needs a New Way to Read OTA Results
item.description: OTAs posted double-digit growth in the latest earnings cycle even as consumer travel spending declined. The industry needs a new framework for reading these results — and the signals that actually matter.

item.title: Has JetBlue’s Transatlantic Growth Hit a Ceiling?
item.description: JetBlue’s transatlantic ambitions are beginning to meet practical limits. Summer 2026 reflects an airline fine-tuning growth as slot constraints, fleet availability, and intensifying competition test its model.

item.title: Meliá’s Upmarket Bet Pays Off in Spain. Cuba Is Another Story
item.description: Meliá is benefiting from Spain’s tourism boom, but Cuba highlights how quickly local conditions can pressure performance.

item.title: Bilt Taps Luxury Hotels to Build Marketplace for Top Spenders
item.description: Bilt is trying to thread a needle in building a hotel booking platform without becoming an OTA that hotels resent. One of its tactics is to offer spending data on its most loyal customers to help luxury hotels provide personalized service for first-time guests.
